$comment: Opt-in variant: merge into the repo's .mcp.json when the repo's tasks genuinely need Jira/Confluence access. uvx-launched (no docker-in-docker). PREREQUISITES — the workload image ships python3 but NO uv/pip, and PyPI is not in the base gateway allowlist, so as shipped this server cannot start; it works only after: (1) add your Atlassian domain PLUS the uvx fetch path — pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org — to the x-extra-allowed-domains anchor in docker-compose.yml (NOT devcontainer.json; the gateway reads that anchor), (2) put uv on PATH in the workload, pinned — e.g. the astral.sh standalone installer at a versioned URL (curl https://astral.sh/uv/<version>/install.sh | sh; also add astral.sh to the anchor — the binary itself comes from GitHub release assets, already base-allowlisted). Remember: credentials come from ~/.agent/agent.env — prefer a scoped service identity (a personal token works; the boot check warns and recommends a service account for unattended fleets); READ_ONLY_MODE is a per-repo decision: keep true for context kits, set false for kits whose job includes updating tickets — the service account's project allowlist is the real boundary.
